216: /// Register a DCR client against the candidate issuer. Returns the client_id
217: /// and the raw registration response for strict-schema inspection.
218: ///
219: /// The client `scope` allow-list is intentionally omitted: the provider
220: /// validates it against supported (OIDC) scopes only, and the CommonCal
221: /// catalog scopes are RESOURCE scopes (declared on the resource server), so
222: /// they cannot appear in the client `scope`. Omitting it lets the client
223: /// request any valid OIDC or resource scope.
224: async fn dcr_register(ctx: &Ctx, redirect: &str) -> Result<(String, Value), String> {
225:     let url = format!("{}/reg", ctx.cfg.issuer);
226:     let payload = json!({
227:         "client_name": "commoncal-lab",
228:         "redirect_uris": [redirect],
229:         "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
230:         "response_types": ["code"],
231:         "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
232:     });
233:     let resp = ctx
234:         .http
235:         .post(&url)
236:         .json(&payload)
237:         .send()
238:         .await
239:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
240:     let status = resp.status();
241:     let body: Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
242:     if !status.is_success() {
243:         return Err(format!("DCR {status}: {}", err_of(&body)));
244:     }
245:     let client_id = body
246:         .get("client_id")
247:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
248:         .ok_or_else(|| "DCR response missing client_id".to_string())?
249:         .to_string();
250:     Ok((client_id, body))
251: }

253: /// Drive the authorization-code flow with S256 PKCE against the candidate
254: /// issuer, through the REAL CommonCal consent flow:
255: ///   auth host -> CommonCal /consent (login decided via session)
256: ///   -> auth host -> CommonCal /consent (consent page rendered)
257: ///   -> POST /consent/decision (approve|deny) -> auth host -> loopback callback
258: ///
259: /// `decision` is "approve" or "deny". Returns (code, state) on approve;
260: /// returns Err on deny (the callback carries an error, not a code).
261: async fn authorize(
262:     ctx: &Ctx,
263:     client_id: &str,
264:     redirect: &str,
265:     scopes: &[String],
266:     resource: &str,
267:     challenge: &str,
268:     state: &str,
269:     decision: &str,
270: ) -> Result<(String, String), String> {
271:     let mut auth_url =
272:         url::Url::parse(&format!("{}/auth", ctx.cfg.issuer)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
273:     auth_url
274:         .query_pairs_mut()
275:         .clear()
276:         .append_pair("client_id", client_id)
277:         .append_pair("redirect_uri", redirect)
278:         .append_pair("response_type", "code")
279:         .append_pair("scope", &scopes.join(" "))
280:         .append_pair("state", state)
281:         .append_pair("code_challenge", challenge)
282:         .append_pair("code_challenge_method", "S256")
283:         .append_pair("resource", resource)
284:         // The provider strips `offline_access` unless the request explicitly
285:         // asks for the consent prompt (check_scope.js). We always want a
286:         // refresh token for the P8/P9/P10 proofs, so request consent.
287:         .append_pair("prompt", "consent");
288: 
289:     // Shared cookie jar (Arc<Jar>) so the login session cookie is presented on
290:     // the consent page. The login client does NOT follow redirects (the 303 to
291:     // `/` would 404 and mask the real login status); the follow client does.
292:     let shared_jar = std::sync::Arc::new(reqwest::cookie::Jar::default());
293: 
294:     let login_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
295:         .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
296:         .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
297:         .cookie_provider(shared_jar.clone())
298:         .build()
299:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
300: 
301:     let follow_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
302:         .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
303:         .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::limited(15))
304:         .cookie_provider(shared_jar.clone())
305:         .build()
306:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
307: 
308:     // Step 1: Login to CommonCal (sets the session cookie in the shared jar).
309:     let commoncal_base = ctx.commoncal_base();
310:     let login_resp = login_client
311:         .post(format!("{commoncal_base}/login"))
312:         .form(&[
313:             ("email", "lab@commoncal.test"),
314:             ("password", "lab-password-123"),
315:             ("continue", "/"),
316:         ])
317:         .send()
318:         .await
319:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
320:     let login_status = login_resp.status();
321:     if !login_status.is_success() && login_status.as_u16() != 303 {
322:         let body = login_resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
323:         return Err(format!(
324:             "CommonCal login failed: {login_status} at {commoncal_base}/login body={body}"
325:         ));
326:     }
327: 
328:     // Step 2: Start the authorization flow. Follow redirects until we reach
329:     // the consent page (200 HTML) or the final callback.
330:     let resp = follow_client
331:         .get(auth_url)
332:         .send()
333:         .await
334:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
335:     let content_type = resp
336:         .headers()
337:         .get("content-type")
338:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
339:         .unwrap_or("")
340:         .to_string();
341:     let status = resp.status();
342:     let final_url = resp.url().to_string();
343:     let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
344: 
345:     // If we landed on the consent page (HTML), parse the CSRF + handoff and
346:     // POST the decision.
347:     if content_type.contains("text/html") && body.contains("consent/decision") {
348:         let handoff = extract_html_value(&body, "handoff")
349:             .ok_or_else(|| "consent page missing handoff".to_string())?;
350:         let csrf = extract_html_value(&body, "csrf")
351:             .ok_or_else(|| "consent page missing csrf".to_string())?;
352: 
353:         let decision_resp = follow_client
354:             .post(format!("{commoncal_base}/consent/decision"))
355:             .form(&[
356:                 ("handoff", handoff.as_str()),
357:                 ("csrf", csrf.as_str()),
358:                 ("decision", decision),
359:             ])
360:             .send()
361:             .await
362:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
363:         // The decision POST returns a 303; reqwest follows the redirect chain
364:         // to the final callback (or an error page).
365:         let final_url = decision_resp.url().to_string();
366:         let final_status = decision_resp.status();
367:         let _ = decision_resp.text().await;
368: 
369:         // The final response should be the loopback callback (or an error).
370:         let cb = url::Url::parse(&final_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
371:         let mut code = None;
372:         let mut state_out = None;
373:         for (k, v) in cb.query_pairs() {
374:             match k.as_ref() {
375:                 "code" => code = Some(v.into_owned()),
376:                 "state" => state_out = Some(v.into_owned()),
377:                 "error" => {
378:                     let desc = cb
379:                         .query_pairs()
380:                         .find(|(kk, _)| kk.as_ref() == "error_description")
381:                         .map(|(_, vv)| vv.into_owned())
382:                         .unwrap_or_default();
383:                     return Err(format!("authorization error at {final_url}: {desc}"));
384:                 }
385:                 _ => {}
386:             }
387:         }
388:         let code = code
389:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing code (status={final_status}): {final_url}"))?;
390:         let state_out = state_out.ok_or_else(|| {
391:             format!("callback missing state (status={final_status}): {final_url}")
392:         })?;
393:         if state_out != state {
394:             return Err(format!("state mismatch: sent {state}, got {state_out}"));
395:         }
396:         return Ok((code, state_out));
397:     }
398: 
399:     // If we didn't land on the consent page, check if we got the callback
400:     // directly (e.g., the consent was auto-decided).
401:     let cb = url::Url::parse(&final_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
402:     let mut code = None;
403:     let mut state_out = None;
404:     for (k, v) in cb.query_pairs() {
405:         match k.as_ref() {
406:             "code" => code = Some(v.into_owned()),
407:             "state" => state_out = Some(v.into_owned()),
408:             "error" => {
409:                 let desc = cb
410:                     .query_pairs()
411:                     .find(|(kk, _)| kk.as_ref() == "error_description")
412:                     .map(|(_, vv)| vv.into_owned())
413:                     .unwrap_or_default();
414:                 return Err(format!("authorization error at {final_url}: {desc}"));
415:             }
416:             _ => {}
417:         }
418:     }
419:     let code =
420:         code.ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing code (status={status}): {final_url}"))?;
421:     let state_out = state_out
422:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing state (status={status}): {final_url}"))?;
423:     if state_out != state {
424:         return Err(format!("state mismatch: sent {state}, got {state_out}"));
425:     }
426:     Ok((code, state_out))
427: }

429: /// Extract a hidden input value from an HTML consent page.
430: /// Looks for: <input type="hidden" name="NAME" value="VALUE">
431: fn extract_html_value(html: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
432:     let needle = format!("name=\"{name}\" value=\"");
433:     let start = html.find(&needle)? + needle.len();
434:     let end = html[start..].find('"')? + start;
435:     Some(html[start..end].to_string())
436: }

518: /// Parse an MCP Streamable-HTTP response body. Handles both `application/json`
519: /// and `text/event-stream` (SSE). For SSE, returns the first `data:` payload
520: /// that is a JSON-RPC response (has `jsonrpc`/`result`/`error`).
521: fn parse_mcp_body(content_type: &str, body: &str) -> Value {
522:     if content_type.contains("text/event-stream") {
523:         for line in body.lines() {
524:             let Some(data) = line.strip_prefix("data:") else {
525:                 continue;
526:             };
527:             let data = data.trim();
528:             if data.is_empty() {
529:                 continue;
530:             }
531:             if let Ok(v) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(data) {
532:                 if v.get("jsonrpc").is_some()
533:                     || v.get("result").is_some()
534:                     || v.get("error").is_some()
535:                 {
536:                     return v;
537:                 }
538:             }
539:         }
540:         Value::Null
541:     } else {
542:         serde_json::from_str(body).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
543:     }
544: }
545: 
546: /// One MCP Streamable-HTTP request. `token` is the RAW access token (no
547: /// "Bearer " prefix). `session` is the `mcp-session-id` from a prior response
548: /// (required after initialize). `id` is `None` for notifications. Returns
549: /// (status, parsed JSON-RPC body, session-id from the response headers).
550: async fn mcp_request(
551:     ctx: &Ctx,
552:     token: Option<&str>,
553:     session: Option<&str>,
554:     id: Option<u32>,
555:     method: &str,
556:     params: Value,
557: ) -> Result<(reqwest::StatusCode, Value, Option<String>), String> {
558:     let mcp = format!("{}/mcp", ctx.cfg.mcp_echo);
559:     let body = match id {
560:         Some(i) => json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": method, "params": params }),
561:         None => json!({ "jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params }),
562:     };
563:     let mut req = ctx
564:         .http
565:         .post(&mcp)
566:         .header("Content-Type", "application/json")
567:         .header("Accept", "application/json, text/event-stream")
568:         .json(&body);
569:     if let Some(t) = token {
570:         req = req.header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {t}"));
571:     }
572:     if let Some(s) = session {
573:         req = req.header("mcp-session-id", s);
574:     }
575:     let resp = req.send().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
576:     let status = resp.status();
577:     let session_id = resp
578:         .headers()
579:         .get("mcp-session-id")
580:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
581:         .map(|s| s.to_string());
582:     let content_type = resp
583:         .headers()
584:         .get("content-type")
585:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
586:         .unwrap_or("")
587:         .to_string();
588:     let body_str = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
589:     let val = parse_mcp_body(&content_type, &body_str);
590:     Ok((status, val, session_id))
591: }

1095: /// Obtain a fresh token (for MCP / refresh / revocation proofs).
1096: async fn fresh_tokens(ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Option<(String, Value)> {
1097:     let redirect = ctx.cfg.loopback_redirect.clone();
1098:     let resource = ctx.cfg.resource_url.clone();
1099:     // Request the catalog (resource) scopes plus offline_access (OIDC) so a
1100:     // refresh token is issued — needed by the P8/P9/P10 proofs.
1101:     let mut scopes: Vec<String> = SCOPE_CATALOG.iter().map(|s| s.to_string()).collect();
1102:     scopes.push("offline_access".to_string());
1103:     let (client_id, _) = match dcr_register(ctx, &redirect).await {
1104:         Ok(v) => v,
1105:         Err(e) => {
1106:             ctx.bad("setup", &format!("DCR failed: {e}"));
1107:             return None;
1108:         }
1109:     };
1110:     let verifier = pkce_verifier();
1111:     let challenge = pkce_challenge(&verifier);
1112:     let (code, _) = match authorize(
1113:         ctx,
1114:         &client_id,
1115:         &redirect,
1116:         &scopes,
1117:         &resource,
1118:         &challenge,
1119:         "fresh-state",
1120:         "approve",
1121:     )
1122:     .await
1123:     {
1124:         Ok(v) => v,
1125:         Err(e) => {
1126:             ctx.bad("setup", &format!("authorize failed: {e}"));
1127:             return None;
1128:         }
1129:     };
1130:     match token_exchange(ctx, &client_id, &redirect, &code, &verifier, &resource).await {
1131:         Ok(t) => Some((client_id, t)),
1132:         Err(e) => {
1133:             ctx.bad("setup", &format!("token exchange failed: {e}"));
1134:             None
1135:         }
1136:     }
1137: }

1139: /// P6: MCP initialize / tools/list / tools/call with a valid token.
1140: async fn mcp_prove(ctx: &mut Ctx) {
1141:     let Some((client_id, tokens)) = fresh_tokens(ctx).await else {
1142:         ctx.bad("P6", "could not obtain a token");
1143:         return;
1144:     };
1145:     let access = tokens
1146:         .get("access_token")
1147:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
1148:         .unwrap_or("")
1149:         .to_string();
1150:     let _ = client_id;
1151: 
1152:     // 1) initialize -> capture the mcp-session-id.
1153:     let init_params = json!({
1154:         "protocolVersion": "2025-03-26",
1155:         "capabilities": {},
1156:         "clientInfo": { "name": "lab-prove", "version": "0.1.0" }
1157:     });
1158:     let session =
1159:         match mcp_request(ctx, Some(&access), None, Some(1), "initialize", init_params).await {
1160:             Ok((status, body, sid)) if status.is_success() && body.get("result").is_some() => {
1161:                 let server_info = body
1162:                     .pointer("/result/serverInfo")
1163:                     .map(|v| v.to_string())
1164:                     .unwrap_or_default();
1165:                 let caps_tools = body.pointer("/result/capabilities/tools").is_some();
1166:                 ctx.ok(
1167:                     "P6",
1168:                     &format!("initialize ok (serverInfo={server_info}, tools_cap={caps_tools})"),
1169:                 );
1170:                 sid
1171:             }
1172:             Ok((status, body, _)) => {
1173:                 ctx.bad("P6", &format!("initialize failed ({status}): {}", body));
1174:                 return;
1175:             }
1176:             Err(e) => {
1177:                 ctx.bad("P6", &format!("initialize transport: {e}"));
1178:                 return;
1179:             }
1180:         };
1181: 
1182:     // 2) notifications/initialized (completes the MCP handshake; no id).
1183:     let _ = mcp_request(
1184:         ctx,
1185:         Some(&access),
1186:         session.as_deref(),
1187:         None,
1188:         "notifications/initialized",
1189:         json!({}),
1190:     )
1191:     .await;
1192: 
1193:     // 3) tools/list (with the session id).
1194:     match mcp_request(
1195:         ctx,
1196:         Some(&access),
1197:         session.as_deref(),
1198:         Some(2),
1199:         "tools/list",
1200:         json!({}),
1201:     )
1202:     .await
1203:     {
1204:         Ok((status, body, _)) => {
1205:             let names: Vec<&str> = body
1206:                 .pointer("/result/tools")
1207:                 .and_then(|v| v.as_array())
1208:                 .map(|a| {
1209:                     a.iter()
1210:                         .filter_map(|t| t.get("name").and_then(|n| n.as_str()))
1211:                         .collect()
1212:                 })
1213:                 .unwrap_or_default();
1214:             let expected: Vec<&str> = vec![
1215:                 "availability_find",
1216:                 "calendar_list",
1217:                 "event_create",
1218:                 "event_get",
1219:                 "event_search",
1220:                 "event_update",
1221:                 "reminder_set",
1222:             ];
1223:             if status.is_success() && names == expected {
1224:                 ctx.ok("P6", &format!("tools/list ok: seven tools {names:?}"));
1225:             } else {
1226:                 ctx.bad("P6", &format!("tools/list wrong ({status}): {body}"));
1227:             }
1228:         }
1229:         Err(e) => ctx.bad("P6", &format!("tools/list transport: {e}")),
1230:     }
1231: 
1232:     // 4) tools/call (with the session id).
1233:     match mcp_request(
1234:         ctx,
1235:         Some(&access),
1236:         session.as_deref(),
1237:         Some(3),
1238:         "tools/call",
1239:         json!({ "name": "calendar_list", "arguments": {} }),
1240:     )
1241:     .await

574:     /// Parse a UTC timestamp (ISO 8601 or Unix epoch) to i64 seconds.
575:     fn parse_ts(s: &str) -> Option<i64> {
576:         if let Ok(ts) = s.parse::<i64>() {
577:             return Some(ts);
578:         }
579:         chrono::DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(s)
580:             .ok()
581:             .map(|dt| dt.timestamp())
582:     }

584:     /// Compute availability slots for a calendar in [from, to].
585:     /// A slot is "busy" if an event overlaps it, otherwise "free".
586:     /// Slots are 1-hour blocks aligned to the hour.
587:     async fn compute_availability(
588:         &self,
589:         calendar_id: i64,
590:         from: &str,
591:         to: &str,
592:     ) -> Vec<serde_json::Value> {
593:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
594:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
595:         let events: Vec<Event> = {
596:             let st = self.inner.read().await;
597:             st.events
598:                 .values()
599:                 .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
600:                 .cloned()
601:                 .collect()
602:         };
603: 
604:         let mut slots = Vec::new();
605:         let mut t = from_ts;
606:         while t < to_ts {
607:             let slot_end = (t + 3600).min(to_ts);
608:             let busy = events.iter().any(|e| {
609:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s < slot_end)
610:                     && e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en > t)
611:             });
612:             slots.push(serde_json::json!({
613:                 "start": t,
614:                 "end": slot_end,
615:                 "status": if busy { "busy" } else { "free" },
616:             }));
617:             t = slot_end;
618:         }
619:         slots
620:     }

631:     /// Search events in a calendar within [from, to], optionally filtered by query.
632:     async fn search_events(
633:         &self,
634:         calendar_id: i64,
635:         from: &str,
636:         to: &str,
637:         query: Option<&str>,
638:     ) -> Vec<Event> {
639:         let from_ts = Self::parse_ts(from).unwrap_or(0);
640:         let to_ts = Self::parse_ts(to).unwrap_or(0);
641:         let st = self.inner.read().await;
642:         let mut results: Vec<Event> = st
643:             .events
644:             .values()
645:             .filter(|e| e.calendar_id == calendar_id)
646:             .filter(|e| {
647:                 e.start_utc.is_some_and(|s| s >= from_ts && s <= to_ts)
648:                     || e.end_utc.is_some_and(|en| en >= from_ts && en <= to_ts)
649:             })
650:             .filter(|e| {
651:                 query.is_none_or(|q| {
652:                     let q_lower = q.to_lowercase();
653:                     e.title
654:                         .as_deref()
655:                         .is_some_and(|t| t.to_lowercase().contains(&q_lower))
656:                         || e.description
657:                             .as_deref()
658:                             .is_some_and(|d| d.to_lowercase().contains(&q_lower))
659:                 })
660:             })
661:             .cloned()
662:             .collect();
663:         drop(st);
664:         results.sort_by_key(|e| e.start_utc.unwrap_or(0));
665:         results
666:     }

862:     /// Look up a handoff from the auth server's private API.
863:     async fn lookup_interaction(&self, handoff: &str) -> Result<InteractionView, String> {

873:             .send()
874:             .await
875:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

878:             let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
879:             tracing::error!(status = %status, body = %body, "lookup_interaction failed");
880:             return Err(format!("interaction lookup failed: {status} {body}"));
881:         }
882:         let body = resp.text().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

888:     /// Decide a handoff (login/consent/deny) via the auth server's private API.
889:     /// `subject` is the authenticated CommonCal user id (the identity authority
890:     /// is CommonCal; the auth server binds the provider grant to this subject
891:     /// rather than a hardcoded value). Returns the resume URL.
892:     ///
893:     /// Honors the lab bridge-failure test hook: if armed, this call fails
894:     /// (simulating a bridge timeout) and the hook decrements, so a retry
895:     /// succeeds — proving grant-first / bridge-second idempotent retry.
896:     async fn decide_interaction(
897:         &self,
898:         handoff: &str,
899:         kind: &str,
900:         subject: Option<i64>,
901:     ) -> Result<String, String> {
902:         // Lab test hook: simulate a bridge failure on the next CONSENT decide
903:         // call(s). Only consent decisions are affected — the grant-first /
904:         // bridge-second ordering is a consent-path property, and login decisions
905:         // must not be disrupted (they precede the grant write).
906:         if kind == "consent" {
907:             let mut st = self.inner.write().await;
908:             if st.decide_fail_remaining > 0 {
909:                 st.decide_fail_remaining -= 1;
910:                 tracing::warn!("simulating bridge decide failure (test hook)");
911:                 return Err("simulated bridge timeout (test hook)".to_string());
912:             }
913:         }
914: 
915:         let url = format!(
916:             "{}/internal/interactions/{}",
917:             self.auth_private_base,
918:             urlencoding::encode(handoff)
919:         );
920:         let mut body = serde_json::json!({ "kind": kind });
921:         if let Some(sub) = subject {
922:             body["subject"] = serde_json::json!(sub);
923:         }
924:         let resp = self
925:             .http
926:             .put(&url)
927:             .header("Authorization", format!("Bearer {}", self.bridge_key))
928:             .json(&body)
929:             .send()
930:             .await
931:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
932:         let status = resp.status();
933:         if !status.is_success() {
934:             let text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
935:             tracing::error!(status = %status, text = %text, "decide_interaction failed");
936:             return Err(format!("interaction decide failed: {status} {text}"));
937:         }
938:         let result: serde_json::Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
939:         result
940:             .get("resumeUrl")
941:             .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
942:             .map(|s| s.to_string())
943:             .ok_or_else(|| "decide response missing resumeUrl".to_string())
944:     }
945: }

960: /// GET /consent?handoff=...
961: ///
962: /// If the interaction prompt is "login" and the user has a session, decide
963: /// login immediately (redirect to resume URL). If the prompt is "consent",
964: /// render the consent page. If no session, redirect to /login.
965: async fn consent_page(
966:     State(state): State<AppState>,
967:     Query(q): Query<ConsentQuery>,
968:     headers: HeaderMap,
969: ) -> Response {
970:     let handoff = match &q.handoff {
971:         Some(h) if !h.is_empty() => h.clone(),
972:         _ => {
973:             return (
974:                 StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
975:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": "missing_handoff"})),
976:             )
977:                 .into_response();
978:         }
979:     };
980: 
981:     // Look up the interaction from the auth server.
982:     let view = match state.lookup_interaction(&handoff).await {
983:         Ok(v) => v,
984:         Err(e) => {
985:             return (
986:                 StatusCode::BAD_GATEWAY,
987:                 Json(serde_json::json!({"error": e})),
988:             )
989:                 .into_response();
990:         }
991:     };
992: 
993:     // Check if the user has a session.
994:     let session_token = extract_session_cookie(&headers);
995:     let user_id = match &session_token {
996:         Some(t) => state.get_session(t).await,
997:         None => None,
998:     };
999: 
1000:     // If no session, redirect to login with a continue param.
1001:     let continue_url = format!("/consent?handoff={}", urlencoding::encode(&handoff));
1002:     let (session_token, user_id) = match (&session_token, user_id) {
1003:         (Some(t), Some(uid)) => (t.clone(), uid),
1004:         _ => {
1005:             let location = format!("/login?continue={}", urlencoding::encode(&continue_url));
1006:             return (StatusCode::SEE_OTHER, [(header::LOCATION, location)]).into_response();
1007:         }

74: impl Config {
75:     /// Parse all configuration from environment variables.
76:     /// Returns raw config without validation.
77:     pub fn parse_env() -> RawConfig {
78:         let app_env = AppEnv::from_env();
79: 
80:         let oauth_issuer = env::var("MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
81:             if app_env == AppEnv::Production {
82:                 String::new()
83:             } else {
84:                 "https://auth.example.com".into()
85:             }
86:         });
87: 
88:         let internal_api_base = env::var("MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
89:             if app_env == AppEnv::Production {
90:                 String::new()
91:             } else {
92:                 "https://commoncal-core.internal".into()
93:             }
94:         });
95: 
96:         let internal_api_key = env::var("MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
97:             if app_env == AppEnv::Production {
98:                 String::new()
99:             } else {
100:                 "mcp-internal-dev-key".into()
101:             }
102:         });
103: 
104:         let session_secret = env::var("MCP_SESSION_SECRET").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
105:             if app_env == AppEnv::Production {
106:                 String::new()
107:             } else {
108:                 "mcp-session-dev-secret-change-in-production".into()
109:             }
110:         });
111: 
112:         let database_path = env::var("MCP_DATABASE_PATH")
113:             .unwrap_or_else(|_| "mcp-server.db".into())
114:             .into();
115: 
116:         let mcp_domain = env::var("MCP_DOMAIN").ok();
117: 
118:         let public_resource_url = env::var("MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL").ok();
119: 
120:         let bind_address = env::var("BIND_ADDRESS").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
121:             if app_env == AppEnv::Production {
122:                 "0.0.0.0:3001".into()
123:             } else {
124:                 "127.0.0.1:3001".into()
125:             }
126:         });
127: 
128:         let dpop_key_path = env::var("DPOP_KEY_PATH").ok().map(PathBuf::from);
129: 
130:         let rate_limit_enabled = env::var("MCP_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED").ok().as_deref() == Some("1");
131: 
132:         let tracing_level = env::var("TRACING_LEVEL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "info".into());
133: 
134:         RawConfig {
135:             app_env,
136:             oauth_issuer,
137:             internal_api_base,
138:             internal_api_key,
139:             session_secret,
140:             database_path,
141:             mcp_domain,
142:             public_resource_url,
143:             bind_address,
144:             dpop_key_path,
145:             rate_limit_enabled,
146:             tracing_level,
147:         }
148:     }
149: 
150:     /// Validate raw configuration. Returns errors for production; returns Config for dev.
151:     pub fn validate(raw: RawConfig) -> Result<Self, Vec<ConfigError>> {
152:         let mut errors = Vec::new();
153: 
154:         // Validate required production fields.
155:         if raw.app_env == AppEnv::Production {
156:             if raw.oauth_issuer.is_empty() {
157:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
158:                     "MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER is required in production",
159:                 ));
160:             } else if raw.oauth_issuer.contains("commoncal.tld") {
161:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
162:                     "MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER must not contain placeholder domain 'commoncal.tld'",
163:                 ));
164:             } else if raw.oauth_issuer.starts_with("http://") {
165:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
166:                     "MCP_OAUTH_ISSUER must use HTTPS in production",
167:                 ));
168:             }
169: 
170:             if raw.internal_api_base.is_empty() {
171:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
172:                     "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE is required in production",
173:                 ));
174:             } else if raw.internal_api_base.contains("commoncal-core.internal") {
175:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
176:                     "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must not contain placeholder domain 'commoncal-core.internal'",
177:                 ));
178:             } else if raw.internal_api_base.starts_with("http://") {
179:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
180:                     "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must use HTTPS in production",
181:                 ));
182:             }
183: 
184:             if raw.internal_api_key.is_empty() {
185:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
186:                     "MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY is required in production",
187:                 ));
188:             } else if raw.internal_api_key == "mcp-internal-dev-key" {
189:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
190:                     "MCP_INTERNAL_API_KEY must not equal development placeholder",
191:                 ));
192:             }
193: 
194:             if raw.session_secret.is_empty() {
195:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
196:                     "MCP_SESSION_SECRET is required in production",
197:                 ));
198:             } else if raw.session_secret.contains("dev-secret") {
199:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
200:                     "MCP_SESSION_SECRET must not contain development placeholder",
201:                 ));
202:             }
203: 
204:             if raw.mcp_domain.as_ref().map_or(true, |d| d.is_empty()) {
205:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new("MCP_DOMAIN is required in production"));
206:             }
207: 
208:             if raw
209:                 .public_resource_url
210:                 .as_ref()
211:                 .map_or(true, |u| u.is_empty())
212:             {
213:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
214:                     "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL is required in production",
215:                 ));
216:             } else if let Some(url_str) = &raw.public_resource_url {
217:                 if let Ok(parsed) = url::Url::parse(url_str) {
218:                     if parsed.scheme() != "https" {
219:                         errors.push(ConfigError::new(
220:                             "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL must use HTTPS in production",
221:                         ));
222:                     }
223:                     if !parsed.username().is_empty() || parsed.password().is_some() {
224:                         errors.push(ConfigError::new(
225:                             "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL must not contain credentials",
226:                         ));
227:                     }
228:                     if parsed.query().is_some() {
229:                         errors.push(ConfigError::new(
230:                             "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL must not contain a query string",
231:                         ));
232:                     }
233:                     if parsed.fragment().is_some() {
234:                         errors.push(ConfigError::new(
235:                             "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL must not contain a fragment",
236:                         ));
237:                     }
238:                     if parsed
239:                         .host_str()
240:                         .map_or(false, |h| h.contains("commoncal.tld"))
241:                     {
242:                         errors.push(ConfigError::new(
243:                             "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL must not contain placeholder domain 'commoncal.tld'",
244:                         ));
245:                     }
246:                 } else {
247:                     errors.push(ConfigError::new(format!(
248:                         "MCP_PUBLIC_RESOURCE_URL '{}' is not a valid URL",
249:                         url_str
250:                     )));
251:                 }
252:             }
253: 
254:             if raw.database_path.as_os_str().is_empty() {
255:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
256:                     "MCP_DATABASE_PATH is required in production",
257:                 ));
258:             }
259: 
260:             if !raw.rate_limit_enabled {
261:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(
262:                     "MCP_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED must be '1' in production",
263:                 ));
264:             }
265:         }
266: 
267:         // Validate bind address in all environments.
268:         let bind_addr = match raw.bind_address.parse::<SocketAddr>() {
269:             Ok(addr) => addr,
270:             Err(e) => {
271:                 errors.push(ConfigError::new(format!(
272:                     "BIND_ADDRESS '{}' is not a valid socket address: {}",
273:                     raw.bind_address, e
274:                 )));
275:                 return Err(errors);
276:             }
277:         };
278: 
279:         if errors.is_empty() {
280:             Ok(Self {
281:                 app_env: raw.app_env,
282:                 oauth_issuer: raw.oauth_issuer,
283:                 internal_api_base: raw.internal_api_base,
284:                 internal_api_key: raw.internal_api_key,
285:                 session_secret: raw.session_secret,
286:                 database_path: raw.database_path,
287:                 mcp_domain: raw.mcp_domain.unwrap_or_default(),
288:                 public_resource_url: raw.public_resource_url.unwrap_or_default(),
289:                 bind_address: bind_addr,
290:                 dpop_key_path: raw.dpop_key_path,
291:                 rate_limit_enabled: raw.rate_limit_enabled,
292:                 tracing_level: raw.tracing_level,
293:             })
294:         } else {
295:             Err(errors)
296:         }
297:     }
298: 
299:     /// Backwards-compatible entry point: parse and validate in one call.
300:     pub fn from_env() -> Result<Self, Vec<ConfigError>> {
301:         let raw = Self::parse_env();
302:         Self::validate(raw)
303:     }
304: }

328: pub struct OauthProtectedResourceMetadata {
329:     pub resource_metadata: Option<String>,
330:     pub resource: String,
331:     pub authorization_servers: Vec<String>,
332:     pub scopes_supported: Vec<String>,
333:     pub dpop_bound_access_tokens: bool,
334: }

336: impl OauthProtectedResourceMetadata {
337:     pub fn new(resource_url: &str, auth_issuer: &str, dpop_supported: bool) -> Self {
338:         let resource_metadata = if resource_url.ends_with("/mcp") || resource_url.ends_with("/mcp/")
339:         {
340:             let stripped = resource_url.trim_end_matches('/');
341:             Some(stripped.replace("/mcp", "/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"))
342:         } else if resource_url.ends_with('/') {
343:             Some(format!("{}oauth-protected-resource", resource_url))
344:         } else {
345:             Some(format!("{}/oauth-protected-resource", resource_url))
346:         };
347:         Self {
348:             resource_metadata,
349:             resource: resource_url.to_string(),
350:             authorization_servers: vec![auth_issuer.to_string()],
351:             scopes_supported: vec![
352:                 "commoncal.calendar.metadata.read".to_string(),
353:                 "commoncal.availability.read".to_string(),
354:                 "commoncal.event.read.basic".to_string(),
355:                 "commoncal.event.read.details".to_string(),
356:                 "commoncal.event.create".to_string(),
357:                 "commoncal.event.update".to_string(),
358:                 "commoncal.event.delete".to_string(),
359:                 "commoncal.reminder.read".to_string(),
360:                 "commoncal.reminder.write".to_string(),
361:             ],
362:             dpop_bound_access_tokens: dpop_supported,
363:         }
364:     }
365: }

85: impl InternalClient {
86:     pub fn new(api_base: String, api_key: String) -> Result<Self, crate::config::ConfigError> {
87:         let url = url::Url::parse(&api_base).map_err(|e| {
88:             crate::config::ConfigError::new(format!(
89:                 "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE is not a valid URL: {}",
90:                 e
91:             ))
92:         })?;
93: 
94:         if !url.username().is_empty() {
95:             return Err(crate::config::ConfigError::new(
96:                 "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must not contain username",
97:             ));
98:         }
99: 
100:         if url.password().is_some() {
101:             return Err(crate::config::ConfigError::new(
102:                 "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must not contain password",
103:             ));
104:         }
105: 
106:         if url.query().is_some_and(|q| !q.is_empty()) {
107:             return Err(crate::config::ConfigError::new(
108:                 "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must not contain query string",
109:             ));
110:         }
111: 
112:         if url.fragment().is_some_and(|f| !f.is_empty()) {
113:             return Err(crate::config::ConfigError::new(
114:                 "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must not contain fragment",
115:             ));
116:         }
117: 
118:         if url.path() != "/" && url.path().ends_with('/') {
119:             return Err(crate::config::ConfigError::new(
120:                 "MCP_INTERNAL_API_BASE must not end with trailing slash",
121:             ));
122:         }
123: 
124:         Ok(Self {
125:             api_base: url,
126:             api_key,
127:             http_client: reqwest::Client::new(),
128:         })
129:     }

139:     /// Perform RFC 8693 token exchange.
140:     ///
141:     /// Converts the MCP client's access_token (issued by the OAuth issuer)
142:     /// into an internal API token that the backend recognizes.
143:     ///
144:     /// Grant type: `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`
145:     /// Subject token: the MCP client's access_token
146:     /// Audience: the internal service name
147:     pub async fn exchange_token(
148:         &self,
149:         subject_token: &str,
150:         actor_token: Option<&str>,
151:         resource: &str,
152:     ) -> Result<TokenExchangeResponse, InternalError> {
153:         let url = self
154:             .api_base
155:             .join("internal/token-exchange")
156:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(format!("failed to join URL: {}", e)))?;
157: 
158:         let mut body = serde_json::json!({
159:             "grant_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange",
160:             "subject_token": subject_token,
161:             "subject_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
162:             "audience": "commoncal-internal",
163:             "resource": [resource],
164:         });
165: 
166:         if let Some(actor) = actor_token {
167:             body["actor_token"] = serde_json::json!(actor);
168:             body["actor_token_type"] =
169:                 serde_json::json!("urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token");
170:         }
171: 
172:         let resp = self
173:             .http_client
174:             .post(url.as_str())
175:             .header("x-mcp-api-key", &self.api_key)
176:             .json(&body)
177:             .send()
178:             .await
179:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(e.to_string()))?;
180: 
181:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
182:             let status = resp.status().as_u16();
183:             let body_text = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_else(|_| "no body".to_string());
184:             tracing::warn!(
185:                 status,
186:                 body = %body_text,
187:                 "token exchange failed"
188:             );
189:             return Err(InternalError::Http(
190:                 status,
191:                 "token exchange failed".to_string(),
192:             ));
193:         }
194: 
195:         let exchange_resp: TokenExchangeResponse = resp
196:             .json()
197:             .await
198:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Deserialize(e.to_string()))?;
199: 
200:         Ok(exchange_resp)
201:     }

548:     /// Resolve the single authoritative MCP grant for a user + OAuth client.
549:     ///
550:     /// CommonCal core is the source of truth for grants. The internal endpoint
551:     /// returns a vector; a well-formed response contains exactly one grant.
552:     /// Zero grants is a normal authorization outcome (`Ok(None)`); more than one
553:     /// is ambiguous core data and fails closed rather than selecting arbitrarily.
554:     pub async fn get_mcp_grant(
555:         &self,
556:         user_id: i64,
557:         client_id: &str,
558:     ) -> Result<Option<McpGrantResponse>, InternalError> {
559:         let mut url = self
560:             .api_base
561:             .join("internal/mcp/mcp-grants")
562:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(format!("failed to join URL: {}", e)))?;
563:         url.query_pairs_mut()
564:             .append_pair("user_id", &user_id.to_string())
565:             .append_pair("client_id", client_id);
566:         let resp = self
567:             .http_client
568:             .get(url.as_str())
569:             .header("x-mcp-api-key", &self.api_key)
570:             .send()
571:             .await
572:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Connection(e.to_string()))?;
573: 
574:         if !resp.status().is_success() {
575:             return Err(InternalError::Http(
576:                 resp.status().as_u16(),
577:                 "get_mcp_grant failed".to_string(),
578:             ));
579:         }
580: 
581:         let grants = resp
582:             .json::<Vec<McpGrantResponse>>()
583:             .await
584:             .map_err(|e| InternalError::Deserialize(e.to_string()))?;
585: 
586:         match grants.len() {
587:             0 => Ok(None),
588:             1 => Ok(Some(grants.into_iter().next().unwrap())),
589:             _ => Err(InternalError::Http(
590:                 500,
591:                 "ambiguous grant response: expected at most one grant".to_string(),
592:             )),
593:         }
594:     }

1: // McpGrant domain model and enforcement.
2: //
3: // The grant is the authoritative permission record for an MCP user + OAuth
4: // client. It is resolved from CommonCal core (the source of truth) through the
5: // internal API and converted into this domain type. Permission checks operate
6: // on the in-memory grant; there is no MCP-local grant table.
7: 
8: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
9: 
10: use crate::internal_client::McpGrantResponse;
11: 
12: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
13: pub struct McpGrant {
14:     pub grant_id: String,
15:     pub user_id: i64,
16:     pub oauth_client_id: String,
17:     pub allowed_calendar_ids: Vec<i64>,
18:     pub allow_availability: bool,
19:     pub allow_event_titles: bool,
20:     pub allow_event_details: bool,
21:     pub allow_create: bool,
22:     pub allow_update: bool,
23:     pub allow_delete: bool,
24:     pub created_at: i64,
25:     pub last_used_at: Option<i64>,
26:     pub expires_at: Option<i64>,
27:     pub revoked_at: Option<i64>,
28: }
29: 
30: /// Convert an authoritative core grant response into the domain type.
31: impl From<McpGrantResponse> for McpGrant {
32:     fn from(response: McpGrantResponse) -> Self {
33:         Self {
34:             grant_id: response.grant_id,
35:             user_id: response.user_id,
36:             oauth_client_id: response.oauth_client_id,
37:             allowed_calendar_ids: response.allowed_calendar_ids,
38:             allow_availability: response.allow_availability,
39:             allow_event_titles: response.allow_event_titles,
40:             allow_event_details: response.allow_event_details,
41:             allow_create: response.allow_create,
42:             allow_update: response.allow_update,
43:             allow_delete: response.allow_delete,
44:             created_at: response.created_at,
45:             last_used_at: response.last_used_at,
46:             expires_at: response.expires_at,
47:             revoked_at: response.revoked_at,
48:         }
49:     }
50: }
51: 
52: /// Check if a calendar is accessible under the grant.
53: ///
54: /// Returns true if:
55: /// - Grant is not revoked
56: /// - Grant is not expired (if expires_at is set)
57: /// - Calendar ID is in the allowed list
58: pub fn check_calendar_access(grant: &McpGrant, calendar_id: i64) -> bool {
59:     if grant.revoked_at.is_some() {
60:         return false;

129:     let jwks = load_jwks(issuer).await?;

132:     let header = parse_jwt_header(token)?;
133: 
134:     // Find the matching key in the JWKS.
135:     let jwk = find_jwk(&jwks, &header.kid)?;

137:     // Convert the JWK to a DecodingKey.
138:     let decoding_key = jwk_to_decoding_key(&jwk)?;

144:     validation.set_audience(&[&audience]);

221:         kid: Option<String>,
222:     }
223: 
224:     let dpop_header: DpopHeader =
225:         serde_json::from_slice(&decoded).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
226: 
227:     // Verify typ is "dpop+jwt".
228:     if dpop_header.typ != "dpop+jwt" {
229:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
230:     }
231: 
232:     // Verify jwk is present (sender-constrained token).
233:     let jwk = dpop_header.jwk.as_ref().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
234: 
235:     // Extract RSA public key from JWK.
236:     let kty = jwk["kty"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
237:     if kty != "RSA" {
238:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
239:     }
240:     let n = jwk["n"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
241:     let e = jwk["e"].as_str().ok_or(TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
242: 
243:     // Determine algorithm (default to RS256 per DPoF spec).
244:     let alg_str = dpop_header.alg.as_deref().unwrap_or("RS256");
245:     let alg = match alg_str {
246:         "RS256" => Algorithm::RS256,
247:         "RS384" => Algorithm::RS384,
248:         "RS512" => Algorithm::RS512,
249:         _ => return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop),
250:     };
251: 
252:     // Construct DecodingKey from JWK.
253:     let decoding_key = DecodingKey::from_rsa_components(n, e).map_err(|e| {
254:         eprintln!(
255:             "DEBUG: from_rsa_components failed: {:?}, n_len={}, e={}",
256:             e,
257:             n.len(),
258:             e
259:         );
260:         TokenError::InvalidDpop
261:     })?;
262: 
263:     // Parse DPoP proof payload.
264:     let payload_b64 = parts[1];
265:     let decoded_payload = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
266:         .decode(payload_b64)
267:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
268: 
269:     #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]
270:     struct DpopClaims {
271:         jti: String,
272:         htm: String,
273:         htu: String,
274:         exp: usize,
275:     }
276: 
277:     let dpop_claims: DpopClaims =
278:         serde_json::from_slice(&decoded_payload).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
279: 
280:     // Verify proof is not expired.
281:     let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
282:         .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
283:         .unwrap()
284:         .as_secs() as usize;
285:     if now >= dpop_claims.exp {
286:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
287:     }
288: 
289:     // Verify the JWS signature against the public key in the DPoP header.
290:     let mut validation = Validation::new(alg);
291:     validation.set_required_spec_claims(&["exp"]);
292:     validation.leeway = 30;
293: 
294:     decode::<DpopClaims>(proof, &decoding_key, &validation).map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidDpop)?;
295: 
296:     // Verify nonce matches (nonce is returned in the response, client must echo it).
297:     if nonce.is_empty() {
298:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidDpop);
299:     }
300: 
301:     Ok(())
302: }

304: /// Load JWKS from the OAuth issuer's well-known endpoint.
305: ///
306: /// Fetches `/.well-known/oauth-jwks` from the issuer URL.
307: /// Caches the result to avoid repeated network calls.
308: pub async fn load_jwks(issuer: &str) -> Result<JwksDocument, TokenError> {
309:     let jwks_url = format!("{}/.well-known/oauth-jwks", issuer);
310: 
311:     // Validate URL to prevent SSRF.
312:     let url = url::Url::parse(&jwks_url)
313:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWKS URL".to_string()))?;
314: 
315:     // Require https scheme.
316:     if url.scheme() != "https" {
317:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
318:             "JWKS URL must use https scheme".to_string(),
319:         ));
320:     }
321: 
322:     // Reject private/resolved hosts.
323:     let host = url
324:         .host_str()
325:         .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("JWKS URL has no host".to_string()))?;
326: 
327:     if is_private_host(host) {
328:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
329:             "JWKS URL points to a private address".to_string(),
330:         ));
331:     }
332: 
333:     // Use a reqwest client with strict TLS settings.
334:     let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
335:         .danger_accept_invalid_certs(false)
336:         .danger_accept_invalid_hostnames(false)
337:         .build()
338:         .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to build HTTP client: {}", e)))?;
339: 
340:     let resp = client
341:         .get(&jwks_url)
342:         .send()
343:         .await
344:         .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to fetch JWKS: {}", e)))?;
345: 
346:     if !resp.status().is_success() {
347:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
348:             "JWKS fetch returned status {}",
349:             resp.status()
350:         )));
351:     }
352: 
353:     let jwks: JwksDocument = resp
354:         .json()
355:         .await
356:         .map_err(|e| TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("failed to parse JWKS: {}", e)))?;
357: 
358:     if jwks.keys.is_empty() {
359:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
360:             "JWKS contains no keys".to_string(),
361:         ));
362:     }
363: 
364:     Ok(jwks)
365: }

367: /// Check if a host string is a private/reserved address.
368: fn is_private_host(host: &str) -> bool {
369:     // Check for localhost variants.
370:     if host == "localhost" || host == "127.0.0.1" || host == "0.0.0.0" || host == "::1" {
371:         return true;
372:     }
373: 
374:     // Check for IPv4 private ranges.
375:     if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<std::net::Ipv4Addr>() {
376:         return ip.is_loopback() || ip.is_unspecified();
377:     }
378: 
379:     // Check for IPv6 private/reserved ranges (fc00::/7).
380:     if let Ok(ip) = host.parse::<std::net::Ipv6Addr>() {
381:         if ip.is_loopback() || ip.is_unspecified() {
382:             return true;
383:         }
384:         // fc00::/7 covers fc00::/8 (ULA) and fe00::/8 (reserved).
385:         let first_byte = ip.octets()[0];
386:         if first_byte == 0xfc || first_byte == 0xfd {
387:             return true;
388:         }
389:         // fe80::/10 (link-local).
390:         if first_byte == 0xfe && (ip.octets()[1] & 0xc0) == 0x80 {
391:             return true;
392:         }
393:     }
394: 
395:     false
396: }

398: /// Parse the JWT header to extract `kid` and `alg`.
399: fn parse_jwt_header(token: &str) -> Result<JwtHeader, TokenError> {
400:     let parts: Vec<&str> = token.split('.').collect();
401:     if parts.len() != 3 {
402:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(
403:             "token must have 3 parts".to_string(),
404:         ));
405:     }
406: 
407:     // Base64url decode the header.
408:     let header_b64 = parts[0];
409:     let decoded = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
410:         .decode(header_b64)
411:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWT header encoding".to_string()))?;
412: 
413:     let header: JwtHeader = serde_json::from_slice(&decoded)
414:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid JWT header JSON".to_string()))?;
415: 
416:     Ok(header)
417: }

419: /// Find a JWK by kid in the JWKS document.
420: fn find_jwk<'a>(jwks: &'a JwksDocument, kid: &'a Option<String>) -> Result<&'a Jwk, TokenError> {
421:     match kid {
422:         Some(kid) => {
423:             jwks.keys.iter().find(|j| j.kid == *kid).ok_or_else(|| {
424:                 TokenError::InvalidToken(format!("no matching key for kid: {}", kid))
425:             })
426:         }
427:         None => {
428:             // If no kid, return the first key (should not happen in production).
429:             jwks.keys
430:                 .first()
431:                 .ok_or_else(|| TokenError::InvalidToken("JWKS contains no keys".to_string()))
432:         }
433:     }
434: }

436: /// Convert a JWK to a jsonwebtoken DecodingKey.
437: fn jwk_to_decoding_key(jwk: &Jwk) -> Result<DecodingKey, TokenError> {
438:     if jwk.kty != "RSA" {
439:         return Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
440:             "unsupported key type: {}, expected RSA",
441:             jwk.kty
442:         )));
443:     }
444: 
445:     // RSA JWK n and e are base64url-encoded big-endian integers.
446:     // Decode to raw bytes and construct a proper SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
447:     let n_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
448:         .decode(&jwk.n)
449:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA modulus encoding".to_string()))?;
450: 
451:     let e_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
452:         .decode(&jwk.e)
453:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA exponent encoding".to_string()))?;
454: 
455:     // Pad modulus to next standard RSA key size (multiple of 128 bytes).
456:     let key_size_bytes = ((n_bytes.len() + 127) / 128) * 128;
457:     let n_padded = if n_bytes.len() < key_size_bytes {
458:         let mut padded = vec![0u8; key_size_bytes - n_bytes.len()];
459:         padded.extend_from_slice(&n_bytes);
460:         padded
461:     } else {
462:         n_bytes
463:     };
464: 
465:     // Construct RSA public key and export to SubjectPublicKeyInfo PEM.
466:     let n_bigint = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&n_padded);
467:     let e_bigint = rsa::BigUint::from_bytes_be(&e_bytes);
468:     let rsa_pubkey = rsa::RsaPublicKey::new(n_bigint, e_bigint)
469:         .map_err(|_| TokenError::InvalidToken("invalid RSA public key components".to_string()))?;
470: 
471:     let pem = rsa_pubkey
472:         .to_public_key_pem(LineEnding::default())
473:         .map_err(|_| {
474:             TokenError::InvalidToken("failed to export RSA public key to PEM".to_string())
475:         })?;
476: 
477:     DecodingKey::from_rsa_pem(pem.into_bytes().as_slice()).map_err(|_| {
478:         TokenError::InvalidToken("failed to decode RSA public key from PEM".to_string())
479:     })
480: }
481: 
482: /// Extract the algorithm from a JWK.
483: fn alg_from_jwk(jwk: &Jwk) -> Result<Algorithm, TokenError> {
484:     match jwk.alg.as_str() {
485:         "RS256" => Ok(Algorithm::RS256),
486:         "RS384" => Ok(Algorithm::RS384),
487:         "RS512" => Ok(Algorithm::RS512),
488:         "ES256" => Ok(Algorithm::ES256),
489:         "ES384" => Ok(Algorithm::ES384),
490:         _ => Err(TokenError::InvalidToken(format!(
491:             "unsupported JWT algorithm: {}",
492:             jwk.alg
493:         ))),
494:     }
495: }

793:         let signature_bytes: Box<[u8]> = signature.into();
794:         let signature_b64 = URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(&signature_bytes);

796:         // Tamper with the payload (change GET to POST in base64url).
797:         // The base64url of "GET" is "R0VU", changing first char to "P" gives "P0VU" which decodes to different bytes.

803:         });

807:         let forged_proof = format!("{}.{}.{}", header_b64, tampered_claims_b64, signature_b64);

809:         // Verify the forged proof is rejected.
810:         let result = rt.block_on(validate_dpop_proof("token", &forged_proof, "nonce"));

1: //! Slice 1 tracer-bullet harness (candidate: `oidc-provider` 9.12.0).
2: //!
3: //! Spawns the disposable lab infra (node auth-server + rmcp mcp-echo), drives
4: //! the full DCR -> S256 PKCE -> cross-host login/consent -> JWT -> MCP chain,
5: //! and asserts each proof item. Prints PASS/FAIL per item and a final summary.
6: //!
7: //! Proven behavior (Slice 1 of the approved plan):
8: //!   P1  strict DCR output (public client, no empty optional fields)
9: //!   P2  DCR redirect rejection (wildcard / malformed / arbitrary HTTPS)
10: //!   P3  S256 PKCE + exact loopback redirect + state round-trip
11: //!   P4  exact JWT claim contract (iss/aud/sub/client_id/scope/jti/iat/exp/amr)
12: //!   P5  consent grants only the requested ∩ catalog intersection
13: //!   P6  authenticated SDK initialize -> tools/list -> calendar_list
14: //!   P7  fail-closed negatives (401 challenge, code replay, missing verifier,
15: //!       wrong audience, wrong resource at token exchange)
16: //!   P8  refresh rotation + replay rejection
17: //!   P9  RFC 7009 revocation
18: //!   P10 provider state persists across an auth-server restart (PostgreSQL)
19: //!
20: //! No real secrets or tokens are printed. Only non-sensitive facts (claim
21: //! names, booleans, counts, statuses) are logged.
22: //!
23: //! Run from the repository root:
24: //!   docker compose -f slice1-lab/compose.yaml up -d postgres
25: //!   cargo build --manifest-path slice1-lab/Cargo.toml --bin mcp-echo --bin lab-prove
26: //!   slice1-lab/target/debug/lab-prove
27: 
28: use base64::Engine;
29: use rand::Rng;
30: use serde_json::{Value, json};
31: use slice1_lab::common::{EVIL_SCOPE, LabConfig, SCOPE_CATALOG, granted_scopes};
32: use slice1_lab::jwt;
33: use std::process::{Child, Command};
34: use std::time::Duration;
35: 
36: struct Ctx {
37:     http: reqwest::Client,
38:     cfg: LabConfig,
39:     pass: u32,
40:     fail: u32,
41:     failures: Vec<String>,
42:     auth_server: Option<Child>,
43:     mcp_echo: Option<Child>,
44:     commoncal: Option<Child>,
45: }
46: 
47: impl Drop for Ctx {
48:     fn drop(&mut self) {
49:         if let Some(mut c) = self.auth_server.take() {
50:             let _ = c.kill();
51:             let _ = c.wait();
52:         }
53:         if let Some(mut c) = self.mcp_echo.take() {
54:             let _ = c.kill();
55:             let _ = c.wait();
56:         }
57:         if let Some(mut c) = self.commoncal.take() {
58:             let _ = c.kill();
59:             let _ = c.wait();
60:         }
61:     }
62: }
63: 
64: impl Ctx {
65:     fn new() -> Self {
66:         Self {
67:             http: reqwest::Client::builder()
68:                 .timeout(Duration::from_secs(15))
69:                 .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
70:                 .cookie_provider(reqwest::cookie::Jar::default().into())
71:                 .build()
72:                 .expect("http client"),
73:             cfg: LabConfig::from_env(),
74:             pass: 0,
75:             fail: 0,
76:             failures: Vec::new(),
77:             auth_server: None,
78:             mcp_echo: None,
79:             commoncal: None,
80:         }
81:     }
82: 
83:     fn ok(&mut self, name: &str, detail: &str) {
84:         self.pass += 1;
85:         println!("PASS  {name}: {detail}");
86:     }
87: 
88:     fn bad(&mut self, name: &str, detail: &str) {
89:         self.fail += 1;
90:         self.failures.push(format!("{name}: {detail}"));
91:         println!("FAIL  {name}: {detail}");
92:     }
93: 
94:     fn lab_root() -> String {
95:         std::env::var("LAB_ROOT").unwrap_or_else(|_| "slice1-lab".to_string())
96:     }
97: 
98:     /// Spawn the node auth-server (public :4000, private :4001, fake CommonCal
99:     /// :4002, loopback callback :8321). Returns the child handle.
100:     fn spawn_auth_server(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
101:         let root = Self::lab_root();
102:         let script = format!("{root}/auth-server/src/server.mjs");
103:         if !std::path::Path::new(&script).exists() {
104:             return Err(format!("auth-server script not found: {script}"));
105:         }
106:         let child = Command::new("node")
107:             .arg(&script)
108:             .env("LAB_ISSUER", &self.cfg.issuer)
109:             .env("LAB_RESOURCE_URL", &self.cfg.resource_url)
110:             .env("LAB_LOOPBACK_REDIRECT", &self.cfg.loopback_redirect)
111:             .env(
112:                 "DATABASE_URL",
113:                 "postgres://oidc:oidc-lab-only@127.0.0.1:5432/oidc",
114:             )
115:             .spawn()
116:             .map_err(|e| format!("spawn node: {e}"))?;
117:         self.auth_server = Some(child);
118:         Ok(())
119:     }
120: 
121:     /// (Re)start the auth-server after killing it (used by P10).
122:     async fn restart_auth_server(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
123:         if let Some(mut c) = self.auth_server.take() {
124:             let _ = c.kill();
125:             let _ = c.wait();
126:         }
127:         // Give the port a moment to be released.
128:         tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300)).await;
129:         self.spawn_auth_server()
130:     }
131: 
132:     fn spawn_mcp_echo(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
133:         let root = Self::lab_root();
134:         let bin = format!("{root}/target/debug/mcp-echo");
135:         if !std::path::Path::new(&bin).exists() {
136:             return Err(format!(
137:                 "mcp-echo binary not found: {bin} (run cargo build first)"
138:             ));
139:         }
140:         let child = Command::new(&bin)
141:             .env("LAB_ISSUER", &self.cfg.issuer)
142:             .env("LAB_RESOURCE_URL", &self.cfg.resource_url)
143:             .env("LAB_MCP_ECHO", &self.cfg.mcp_echo)
144:             .env("MCP_ECHO_COMMONCAL", &self.commoncal_base())
145:             .env("MCP_ECHO_BRIDGE_KEY", "slice1-loopback-bridge-key")
146:             .spawn()
147:             .map_err(|e| format!("spawn mcp-echo: {e}"))?;
148:         self.mcp_echo = Some(child);
149:         Ok(())
150:     }
151: 
152:     /// The CommonCal lab service base URL (loopback).
153:     fn commoncal_base(&self) -> String {
154:         std::env::var("LAB_COMMONCAL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "http://127.0.0.1:4002".to_string())
155:     }
156: 
157:     fn spawn_commoncal(&mut self) -> Result<(), String> {
158:         let root = Self::lab_root();
159:         let bin = format!("{root}/target/debug/commoncal");
160:         if !std::path::Path::new(&bin).exists() {
161:             return Err(format!(
162:                 "commoncal binary not found: {bin} (run cargo build first)"
163:             ));
164:         }
165:         let child = Command::new(&bin)
166:             .env("COMMONCAL_AUTH_PRIVATE", "http://127.0.0.1:4001")
167:             .env("COMMONCAL_BRIDGE_KEY", "slice1-loopback-bridge-key")
168:             .env("COMMONCAL_BIND", "127.0.0.1:4002")
169:             .spawn()
170:             .map_err(|e| format!("spawn commoncal: {e}"))?;
171:         self.commoncal = Some(child);
172:         Ok(())
173:     }
174: 
175:     async fn wait_healthy(&self, url: &str, what: &str) -> bool {
176:         for _ in 0..120 {
177:             if self
178:                 .http
179:                 .get(url)
180:                 .send()
181:                 .await
182:                 .map(|r| r.status().is_success())
183:                 .unwrap_or(false)
184:             {
185:                 return true;
186:             }
187:             tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(250)).await;
188:         }
189:         eprintln!("FATAL: {what} not healthy at {url}");
190:         false
191:     }
192: }
193: 
194: fn pkce_verifier() -> String {
195:     const ALPHABET: &[u8] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-._~";
196:     let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();
197:     (0..64)
198:         .map(|_| ALPHABET[rng.gen_range(0..ALPHABET.len())] as char)
199:         .collect()
200: }
201: 
202: fn pkce_challenge(verifier: &str) -> String {
203:     use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
204:     let digest = Sha256::digest(verifier.as_bytes());
205:     base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(digest)
206: }
207: 
208: fn err_of(body: &Value) -> String {
209:     body.get("error_description")
210:         .or_else(|| body.get("error"))
211:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
212:         .unwrap_or("unknown")
213:         .to_string()
214: }
215: 
216: /// Register a DCR client against the candidate issuer. Returns the client_id
217: /// and the raw registration response for strict-schema inspection.
218: ///
219: /// The client `scope` allow-list is intentionally omitted: the provider
220: /// validates it against supported (OIDC) scopes only, and the CommonCal
221: /// catalog scopes are RESOURCE scopes (declared on the resource server), so
222: /// they cannot appear in the client `scope`. Omitting it lets the client
223: /// request any valid OIDC or resource scope.
224: async fn dcr_register(ctx: &Ctx, redirect: &str) -> Result<(String, Value), String> {
225:     let url = format!("{}/reg", ctx.cfg.issuer);
226:     let payload = json!({
227:         "client_name": "commoncal-lab",
228:         "redirect_uris": [redirect],
229:         "grant_types": ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
230:         "response_types": ["code"],
231:         "token_endpoint_auth_method": "none"
232:     });
233:     let resp = ctx
234:         .http
235:         .post(&url)
236:         .json(&payload)
237:         .send()
238:         .await
239:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
240:     let status = resp.status();
241:     let body: Value = resp.json().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
242:     if !status.is_success() {
243:         return Err(format!("DCR {status}: {}", err_of(&body)));
244:     }
245:     let client_id = body
246:         .get("client_id")
247:         .and_then(|v| v.as_str())
248:         .ok_or_else(|| "DCR response missing client_id".to_string())?
249:         .to_string();
250:     Ok((client_id, body))
251: }
252: 
253: /// Drive the authorization-code flow with S256 PKCE against the candidate
254: /// issuer, through the REAL CommonCal consent flow:
255: ///   auth host -> CommonCal /consent (login decided via session)
256: ///   -> auth host -> CommonCal /consent (consent page rendered)
257: ///   -> POST /consent/decision (approve|deny) -> auth host -> loopback callback
258: ///
259: /// `decision` is "approve" or "deny". Returns (code, state) on approve;
260: /// returns Err on deny (the callback carries an error, not a code).
261: async fn authorize(
262:     ctx: &Ctx,
263:     client_id: &str,
264:     redirect: &str,
265:     scopes: &[String],
266:     resource: &str,
267:     challenge: &str,
268:     state: &str,
269:     decision: &str,
270: ) -> Result<(String, String), String> {
271:     let mut auth_url =
272:         url::Url::parse(&format!("{}/auth", ctx.cfg.issuer)).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
273:     auth_url
274:         .query_pairs_mut()
275:         .clear()
276:         .append_pair("client_id", client_id)
277:         .append_pair("redirect_uri", redirect)
278:         .append_pair("response_type", "code")
279:         .append_pair("scope", &scopes.join(" "))
280:         .append_pair("state", state)
281:         .append_pair("code_challenge", challenge)
282:         .append_pair("code_challenge_method", "S256")
283:         .append_pair("resource", resource)
284:         // The provider strips `offline_access` unless the request explicitly
285:         // asks for the consent prompt (check_scope.js). We always want a
286:         // refresh token for the P8/P9/P10 proofs, so request consent.
287:         .append_pair("prompt", "consent");
288: 
289:     // Shared cookie jar (Arc<Jar>) so the login session cookie is presented on
290:     // the consent page. The login client does NOT follow redirects (the 303 to
291:     // `/` would 404 and mask the real login status); the follow client does.
292:     let shared_jar = std::sync::Arc::new(reqwest::cookie::Jar::default());
293: 
294:     let login_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
295:         .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
296:         .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::none())
297:         .cookie_provider(shared_jar.clone())
298:         .build()
299:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
300: 
301:     let follow_client = reqwest::Client::builder()
302:         .timeout(Duration::from_secs(20))
303:         .redirect(reqwest::redirect::Policy::limited(15))
304:         .cookie_provider(shared_jar.clone())
305:         .build()
306:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
307: 
308:     // Step 1: Login to CommonCal (sets the session cookie in the shared jar).
309:     let commoncal_base = ctx.commoncal_base();
310:     let login_resp = login_client
311:         .post(format!("{commoncal_base}/login"))
312:         .form(&[
313:             ("email", "lab@commoncal.test"),
314:             ("password", "lab-password-123"),
315:             ("continue", "/"),
316:         ])
317:         .send()
318:         .await
319:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
320:     let login_status = login_resp.status();
321:     if !login_status.is_success() && login_status.as_u16() != 303 {
322:         let body = login_resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
323:         return Err(format!(
324:             "CommonCal login failed: {login_status} at {commoncal_base}/login body={body}"
325:         ));
326:     }
327: 
328:     // Step 2: Start the authorization flow. Follow redirects until we reach
329:     // the consent page (200 HTML) or the final callback.
330:     let resp = follow_client
331:         .get(auth_url)
332:         .send()
333:         .await
334:         .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
335:     let content_type = resp
336:         .headers()
337:         .get("content-type")
338:         .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
339:         .unwrap_or("")
340:         .to_string();
341:     let status = resp.status();
342:     let final_url = resp.url().to_string();
343:     let body = resp.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
344: 
345:     // If we landed on the consent page (HTML), parse the CSRF + handoff and
346:     // POST the decision.
347:     if content_type.contains("text/html") && body.contains("consent/decision") {
348:         let handoff = extract_html_value(&body, "handoff")
349:             .ok_or_else(|| "consent page missing handoff".to_string())?;
350:         let csrf = extract_html_value(&body, "csrf")
351:             .ok_or_else(|| "consent page missing csrf".to_string())?;
352: 
353:         let decision_resp = follow_client
354:             .post(format!("{commoncal_base}/consent/decision"))
355:             .form(&[
356:                 ("handoff", handoff.as_str()),
357:                 ("csrf", csrf.as_str()),
358:                 ("decision", decision),
359:             ])
360:             .send()
361:             .await
362:             .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
363:         // The decision POST returns a 303; reqwest follows the redirect chain
364:         // to the final callback (or an error page).
365:         let final_url = decision_resp.url().to_string();
366:         let final_status = decision_resp.status();
367:         let _ = decision_resp.text().await;
368: 
369:         // The final response should be the loopback callback (or an error).
370:         let cb = url::Url::parse(&final_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
371:         let mut code = None;
372:         let mut state_out = None;
373:         for (k, v) in cb.query_pairs() {
374:             match k.as_ref() {
375:                 "code" => code = Some(v.into_owned()),
376:                 "state" => state_out = Some(v.into_owned()),
377:                 "error" => {
378:                     let desc = cb
379:                         .query_pairs()
380:                         .find(|(kk, _)| kk.as_ref() == "error_description")
381:                         .map(|(_, vv)| vv.into_owned())
382:                         .unwrap_or_default();
383:                     return Err(format!("authorization error at {final_url}: {desc}"));
384:                 }
385:                 _ => {}
386:             }
387:         }
388:         let code = code
389:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing code (status={final_status}): {final_url}"))?;
390:         let state_out = state_out.ok_or_else(|| {
391:             format!("callback missing state (status={final_status}): {final_url}")
392:         })?;
393:         if state_out != state {
394:             return Err(format!("state mismatch: sent {state}, got {state_out}"));
395:         }
396:         return Ok((code, state_out));
397:     }
398: 
399:     // If we didn't land on the consent page, check if we got the callback
400:     // directly (e.g., the consent was auto-decided).
401:     let cb = url::Url::parse(&final_url).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
402:     let mut code = None;
403:     let mut state_out = None;
404:     for (k, v) in cb.query_pairs() {
405:         match k.as_ref() {
406:             "code" => code = Some(v.into_owned()),
407:             "state" => state_out = Some(v.into_owned()),
408:             "error" => {
409:                 let desc = cb
410:                     .query_pairs()
411:                     .find(|(kk, _)| kk.as_ref() == "error_description")
412:                     .map(|(_, vv)| vv.into_owned())
413:                     .unwrap_or_default();
414:                 return Err(format!("authorization error at {final_url}: {desc}"));
415:             }
416:             _ => {}
417:         }
418:     }
419:     let code =
420:         code.ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing code (status={status}): {final_url}"))?;
421:     let state_out = state_out
422:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("callback missing state (status={status}): {final_url}"))?;
423:     if state_out != state {
424:         return Err(format!("state mismatch: sent {state}, got {state_out}"));
425:     }
426:     Ok((code, state_out))
427: }

438: /// Exchange the authorization code for tokens. `resource` is the exact RFC 8707
439: /// resource (sent again at token exchange to prove the provider enforces it).
440: async fn token_exchange(
441:     ctx: &Ctx,
442:     client_id: &str,
443:     redirect: &str,
444:     code: &str,
445:     verifier: &str,
446:     resource: &str,
447: ) -> Result<Value, String> {
448:     let url = format!("{}/token", ctx.cfg.issuer);
449:     let form = [
450:         ("grant_type", "authorization_code"),
451:         ("code", code),
452:         ("redirect_uri", redirect),
453:         ("client_id", client_id),
454:         ("code_verifier", verifier),
455:         ("resource", resource),
456:     ];
457:     let resp = ctx
458:         .http
459:         .post(&url)
460:         .form(&form)
461:         .send()
462:         .await

466:     if !status.is_success() {
467:         return Err(format!("token {status}: {}", err_of(&body)));
468:     }
469:     Ok(body)
